THE VERSION OF YOU THAT THOUGHT IT WAS OVER

lines: If Christ was crucified 2,000 years ago, then why does Paul say, "I am crucified with Christ"?
Not was. Am.
Galatians 2. "I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me."
Christ lives in him.
Paul says it again in Colossians. "Christ in you, the hope of glory."
In the last two parts we saw it. The cry on the cross is David's.
David is God's son, the anointed one, the Christ.
And David stands for all of us. Humanity.
So the Christ that hangs on that cross is called man.
And that cry is the cry of every man, woman and child ever nailed to a cross.
How many times have you felt like the world was ending?
Like all the walls were closing in?
Like you cried out and heaven went quiet?
You are the one on the cross. You are the one hung on the tree as a sacrifice.
Peter says He "bare our sins in his own body on the tree."
And Paul says, "Our old man is crucified with him."
So what's being sacrificed up there? The old man. The one who believed he was forsaken.
And here's what the crowd never heard. Psalm 22 doesn't end where it starts. It turns.
"When he cried unto him, he heard."
And it ends, "He hath done this."
The son cries out. The father hears. It is finished.
Tonight, if you're on the cross, say the cry. Be honest about it.
Then name what's dying: the fear, the old story, the version of you that thought it was over.
Let it go.
Then say the last line like you've already seen it: He hath done this.
Comment temple and I'll send you the app for the nights the walls close in.
Why does Paul say "I am crucified"? Because the cross was never 2,000 years ago.
It's where you are right now. And so is the resurrection.
